topic: Honeykrisp ~28-30 us per-dispatch floor on the M1: attribution via a minimal Vulkan microbenchmark, a per-launch CDM-barrier driver patch, and digest-gated correctness
host: jwm1-linux, Apple M1 (G13G B1), linux-asahi 7.1.6, glslc; dev box for prep only
baseline_question: receipts/2026-09-09-decode-fusion/floor.json reported ~29.9 us GPU + ~20.5 us gap per one-workgroup dispatch (~50 us wall) as the Q4 decode floor, with barriers, host descriptor cost, and submission count already ruled out.

instrument.what: tools/dispatch-floor-bench (this branch): minimal Vulkan compute microbenchmark; empty vs trivial vs no-side-effect kernels; sweeps dispatch count (64-4096), workgroup size (32-512), Vulkan barriers, descriptor rebinding, push-constant updates, pipeline switching, per-dispatch timestamp brackets, and one-dispatch-per-submit round trips; NDJSON out; host CLOCK_MONOTONIC is the absolute scale (device timestamp periods are not trustworthy, see receipts/2026-09-10-q4-gemv-bandwidth/verdict.json).
instrument.note: empty shaders are skipped by hk dispatch() (agx_is_shader_empty), so empty cases measure host recording only; nop (always-false store) is the true zero-work launch.

floor_verdict.comparison_stock_mesa_26_1_7: every case within noise of the fork (trivial 4.52 vs 4.52; table in artifacts dfb-6f6afc8-*.ndjson)
floor_verdict.reading: The real per-dispatch floor through Honeykrisp on this M1 is ~4.5 us in a tightly pre-recorded chain: ~2.5 us device CDM launch-to-launch cadence (nop == trivial: independent of memory writes) plus ~2 us host record. Vulkan memory barriers, descriptor rebinding, push-constant updates, and pipeline switching are all free inside a chain.

28_30us_floor_explained.reading: Bracketing every dispatch with timestamps costs ~21-23 us per bracket pair on both fork and stock - matching the 25.3/29.9 us one-workgroup GPU times in receipts/2026-09-10-decode-bound-3 and floor.json almost exactly. The previously reported per-dispatch floor was the profiling instrument, not the driver or the hardware. Any future profile must anchor brackets hundreds of dispatches apart, not per dispatch.

driver_patch.branch: hk/cdm-barrier-floor (joshuaswarren/mesa, based on honeykrisp-omarchy 6f6afc8 = installed pkg mesa-honeykrisp-omarchy 26.3.0.devel.hk6f6afc8)
driver_patch.change: HK_PERFTEST=nocdmbarrier (omit the per-launch kitchen-sink CDM_BARRIER), HK_PERFTEST=usccdmbarrier (reduce it to usc_cache_inval); new agx_cdm_barrier_usc in libagx; default emission byte-identical to before.
driver_patch.why_not_default_change: The kitchen-sink per-launch barrier is a measured no-op for throughput (nocdmbarrier leaves every microbenchmark case unchanged), so there is nothing to win - but it is load-bearing for correctness: under HK_PERFTEST=nocdmbarrier the omarchy runtime suite fails 4/41 cases with 6254 failed assertions (query/GPU-CPU coherency paths depend on it). Keeping the default is the only correct choice.
driver_patch.measured_no_op_evidence: dfb-6f6afc8-DEFAULT vs dfb-6f6afc8-NOCDMBARRIER: trivial_1wg 4.52 us both; all cases within noise.

digest_gate.status: FAILED for worktree-built drivers; canonical digests reproduce only under the installed package

evidence.installed_pkg_same_commit: QmmAlignDeterminism window C on the same host reproduced all six canonical pins during this run (their receipt)

digest_gate.implication: Driver A/B at digest level requires the package build recipe (PKGBUILD flags), not an ad-hoc meson config: shader/kernel selection or codegen is build-sensitive. This is a standalone finding: never gate digests on ad-hoc driver builds. My patch's default mode is byte-identical CS emission, so it cannot change arithmetic by construction; but the honest gate statement is 'not reproducible under worktree builds', not 'digests verified'.

decode_implication.reading: With the true floor at ~4.5 us and 273 dispatches per token, launch overhead is ~1.2 ms of an ~8.9 ms release-wheel token (paired-barriers receipt), and the real levers remain the q4 kernel chain time and the ~7.3 ms of host-paced intra-submission gaps in the diagnostics view - not a driver dispatch floor. The Q4 parity blocker is not Honeykrisp dispatch overhead.

ml_repo_hygiene: No mlx-omarchy main merge: bench + receipt live on branch wave/DispatchFloor; driver patch on hk/cdm-barrier-floor.
